raw_response:
I have farmed a long time, and on 12 mu with a wheat-maize rotation and well irrigation, I would keep things simple, steady, and labor-conscious. Some people in my family work off-farm, so I would not spread myself too thin with too much cotton because cotton takes more hand work and management over a long season. I would put most of my land into the wheat-maize rotation because that fits my land, my experience, and my irrigation conditions, and it gives me more stable grain output. I would still keep a smaller cotton area because I know how to grow it and it helps me keep some cash-crop income, but I would not expand it. For wheat, I would use improved seed, moderate fertilizer, and two irrigations because I have wells and I want steady establishment, winter survival, and grain filling. For summer maize, I would use hybrid seed because that is what I would trust most for yield, and I would give it enough nitrogen and one to two irrigations depending on rain; with well water available, I would plan on two to be safe. For cotton, I would use improved seed, fertilize moderately, irrigate a few times, and manage pests more carefully than grain crops because that is where cotton can easily lose yield. I would mostly use rotary tillage because it saves labor and matches how I would manage a small farm at my age. Overall, I would aim for reliable production instead of chasing the highest possible yield, because I care more about finishing the season safely, on time, and with a stable return.
